title: The Evolution of Islamic Finance: Contractual Continuity, Institutional Transformation, and the Search for Sharia Substance

summary: Islamic finance has expanded from classical trade-based mechanisms into a global financial architecture with total assets exceeding US$3 trillion. We introduce a five-dimensional analytical framework, comparing Classical Foundations, Modern Forms, Continuity Mechanisms, Transformation Dynamics, and Sharia/Ethical Implications, to examine how classical contracts (Mudarabah, Musharakah, Bay’ al-Salam) have evolved into modern capital market instruments (Sukuk, Takaful, trade finance). summary: This paper revisits Keynes's socialization of investment and asks what institutional form it might take in the face of the climate crisis.
